source_name: EY Slovakia / Big Four SK insight pages on IT & tech transactions
why_relevant: Consultancy commentary on the Slovak IT/tech transaction market, incl. financial-sector technology deals; gives market framing and occasionally names deal activity not covered by media.

source_name: MIRRI SR – Plán obnovy a odolnosti (recovery plan section, Komponent 17 Digitálne Slovensko)
why_relevant: MIRRI is the implementing body for RRF Component 17 (Digitálne Slovensko). Its recovery-plan section publishes calls, milestones and project lists months before the corresponding tenders reach the public procurement journal, effectively pre-announcing which payment/e-government systems will be procured.

source_name: planobnovy.sk – official Recovery and Resilience Plan portal (full plan text + component pages)
why_relevant: Holds the complete RRP text and the 'Efektívna verejná správa a digitalizácia' component page, plus the methodological guide for IT in the RRP. Naming of planned systems here precedes tender publication by many months.

source_name: Eurofondy.gov.sk – Výzvy Programu Slovensko 2021–2027
why_relevant: Central listing of EU-funded calls, including measures 1.2.1/1.2.2/1.4.2/1.5.1 covering informatization, digital transformation and cybersecurity. Awarded grants convert into procurement by the beneficiary institutions, so this is a lead indicator of forthcoming IT/payments tenders.

source_name: MIRRI – Výzvy sekcie informatizácie (dotácie / IT calls)
why_relevant: Section-level call list of the informatization branch; smaller and faster-moving than the eurofondy portal and often the first place a planned system is named.

source_name: MetaIS – Centrálny metainformačný systém verejnej správy (public register of state IT assets and projects)
why_relevant: The authoritative register of ISVS (public administration information systems), project records, feasibility studies, TCO and architecture. A new project record in MetaIS typically exists well before the tender notice; searching for payment-related ISVS reveals which institutions plan payment system work.

source_name: MIRRI – Verejné pripomienkovanie projektovej dokumentácie / štúdií uskutočniteľnosti
why_relevant: Mandatory public consultation of project documentation and feasibility studies for state IT projects. Each notice names the planned system, scope, indicative budget and architecture — the single strongest pre-tender signal in the Slovak public sector.

source_name: Ministerstvo financií SR – Útvar hodnoty za peniaze, hodnotenia investičných projektov (IT)
why_relevant: By law (523/2004 §19a) IT investments above ~EUR 10m must be economically assessed by ÚHP BEFORE public procurement starts. The published evaluation PDFs name the system, scope, cost model and expected procurement route — a legally guaranteed pre-tender artefact.

source_name: MF SR – projektové zámery informatizácie (manažérske výstupy I-02, e.g. eFaktúra)
why_relevant: Concrete example of a published 'projektový zámer' for the eFaktúra (e-invoicing) project — a payments-adjacent state system. Such I-02 documents specify modules, integration points and indicative procurement lots long before tender.

source_name: Slovensko.Digital – odporúčania k novým projektom a obstarávaniam (recommendation papers)
why_relevant: Position/recommendation documents on upcoming projects and procurements enumerate planned tenders and their contested points; useful for anticipating scope changes and delays.

source_name: ITAPA – congress programme and partner listings (Jarná ITAPA / ITAPA Health & Care)
why_relevant: Slovakia's flagship public-sector technology congress. Session titles and panellists reveal which institutions are planning which systems (e.g. a 2026 panel on state digitalisation of the payment-to-invoice flow featuring Finančná správa, the Slovak Banking Association and Štátna pokladnica). Partner/sponsor lists show which vendors are courting which institution.

source_name: FinReport.sk – fintech / conference coverage
why_relevant: Trade media that reports conference agendas and panel content in detail, often naming institutions and planned systems that are otherwise buried in slide decks. Useful as a discovery layer for events and speakers.

source_name: IBV NBS – FinNext conference (Inštitút bankového vzdelávania NBS)
why_relevant: Central-bank-affiliated financial-sector conference; speaker rosters mix NBS payment-systems staff, bank executives and fintech vendors, revealing which technology themes and suppliers the sector is engaging before procurement.

source_name: Národná banka Slovenska – Konferencie a podujatia
why_relevant: NBS event calendar; workshops on payment systems (SIPS, TARGET-SK, instant payments, digital euro) signal upcoming infrastructure changes that force banks and the state to procure.

source_name: NBS – payment systems strategy news (oddelenie stratégie platobných systémov)
why_relevant: Statements by the head of the NBS payment systems strategy department pre-announce timelines (digital euro pilot 2027, full rollout 2029; opening payment systems to non-bank PSPs). These timelines drive bank and state IT procurement 12-36 months ahead.

source_name: Profesia.sk – job board (procurement / payments / vendor management roles)
why_relevant: Dominant Slovak job board. Postings for 'špecialista verejného obstarávania', payments product owners, core-banking or card-platform roles at banks and state agencies are a classic weak signal that a programme is being staffed ahead of tender.

source_name: Bank career portals – Slovenská sporiteľňa, VÚB, Tatra banka/Raiffeisen, SZRB
why_relevant: Direct-from-employer vacancy lists. A cluster of payments/core-banking/vendor-management or procurement hires at a specific bank is an early indicator of a platform programme. SZRB (state guarantee & development bank) even posts a dedicated public-procurement specialist role, confirming in-house tender activity.

source_name: MIRRI – Centrálne projekty MIRRI SR a správa architektúry (NKIVS / architecture documents)
why_relevant: Architecture-governance pages listing central projects and the enterprise architecture of the state. Strategy/architecture documents name planned systems and integration platforms years ahead of procurement.

source_name: MIRRI – Inštitút digitálnych a regionálnych politík: investície / prioritisation methodology
why_relevant: The analytical unit publishes the investment prioritisation methodology (>EUR 1m threshold) and investment outputs — showing which projects are queued and in what order, i.e. the shape of the tender pipeline.

source_name: Finančná správa SR – eFaktúra and QR/instant-payment (NOP) programme pages
why_relevant: The tax administration's e-invoicing and QR/instant-payment notifier (NOP, built with STU) programmes create downstream procurement for certified delivery providers ('digitálny poštár'), POS/ORP integration and bank connectivity. Programme pages give timelines and accreditation requirements before the related tenders.

source_name: MIRRI – call for expert evaluators of IT projects (Program Slovensko)
why_relevant: Recruitment of external evaluators for measures 1.2.1/1.2.2/1.4.2/1.5.1 is itself a staffing signal that a wave of IT grant decisions — and consequent procurements — is imminent, and it names the exact measures involved.

source_name: Slovak Fintech Association – Eventy
why_relevant: Event listing for the Slovak fintech community; useful pointer to vendor days, meetups and bank-hosted innovation events where suppliers are courted before formal RFPs.

source_name: SBA – Slovenská banková asociácia (news / positions)
why_relevant: Sector body whose staff appear on state digitalisation panels (e.g. the ITAPA payment-to-invoice panel). Its news and position papers reveal which shared payment infrastructure the banking sector is preparing to build or co-fund.

source_name: CRZ bulk export — denné zmenové dávky (XML/ZIP)
why_relevant: Machine-readable daily change batches of the whole CRZ in XML packed as ZIP, documented on the national open-data catalogue (formerly data.gov.sk/dataset/crz, now redirecting to data.slovensko.sk). Documented download pattern http://www.crz.gov.sk/export/rrrr-mm-dd.zip with stated crawl limits (roughly 1 request / 2 s daytime 06:00-20:00, under 3 req/s at night). This is the backbone for building a longitudinal SK banking/payments public-spend dataset rather than ad-hoc searching.
